note: Rewritten from the species-level Diagnostic characters in State Fauna Series 8, Fauna of Gujarat, the original in English. The original records the species as published by Roonwal 1953 (Indian J. Ent. 15(2): 115—118, holotype soldier in the AMNH), type locality Almora, Uttar Pradesh, India (printed as Alniora in the OCR). OCR problems: the sentence on the worker mandibular teeth is fragmentary (left mandible; l sl marginal ... 3 rd / Right 1 M marginal ...) and can only be restored from the context; the tooth counts given (3 left, 3 right) rest on the surviving apical + 2 marginal phrases and on the context. The Gujarat material was collected together with Microtermes obesi.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown, body pale yellow; mandibles dark brown. Body length 4.9—6.0 mm. Head capsule subrectangular; head length without the mandibles 1.50—1.78 mm, width 0.97—1.05 mm. Fontanelle minute, circular. Mandibles sabre-shaped, 0.90—1.05 mm long, incurved at the tip; the base of the left mandible with a blunt projection, the broad base with several fine striae. Antennae 12—17-segmented (mostly 14—15); segment 2 nearly as long as segments 3 and 4 together; segment 3 shortest. Postmentum long, clavate; length 1.13—1.50 mm, greatest width 0.30—0.38 mm, waist width 0.13—0.19 mm. Legs slender; apical tibial spur formula 3:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate oval.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale yellow, body paler. Body length 4.5—6.00 mm. Head capsule nearly square; width 0.86—1.14 mm. Antennae 13—16-segmented (mostly 15). Postclypeus weakly raised. Mandible tips finger-like; left mandible with the 1st marginal tooth slightly smaller than the apical tooth, the 2nd marginal tooth nearly as long as the apical tooth, the 3rd marginal tooth short; right mandible with the 1st marginal tooth small and reduced, situated at the anterior base of the 2nd marginal tooth, the 2nd marginal tooth triangular, the 3rd marginal tooth short.
